AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim in substance: the sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation IS construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (skulking_colony.py:29-33). The game runs it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded (CombatManager.cs:860-867) inside StartCombatInternal (CombatManager.cs:393-398), i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart. Same observable today on all three of section 2's clauses (listener set / HP-roll inversion / roll ordering); the concrete trigger that would make it a gap is a relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Rule 7: the four relic files and sts2_rl/powers.py that section 2's clause (a)/(b) argument cites are NOT hashed by this record. Here the effect is PowerCmd.Apply<HardenedShellPower>(Creature, 20m, Creature) (SkulkingColony.cs:53-57) -> PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, HardenedShellPower, 20). Self-applied, no card, amount is a literal 20 that reads no HP, so none of section 2's three clauses bites.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node identical to SkulkingColony.cs:59-75. Four MoveStates, a pure deterministic chain, no branch state at all: ZOOM_MOVE -> ZOOM_MOVE_2 -> INERTIA_MOVE -> PIERCING_STABS_MOVE -> ZOOM_MOVE, initial ZOOM_MOVE. Executed (monster_probes_b04.py graphs): identical edge set and identical opening move. The two ZOOM states share one delegate on both sides and differ only by id, which per SHARED-FINDINGS section 3 is internal.

guards.rationale: SkulkingColony.cs:77-84 awaits the DamageCmd first and then PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>, so the +2 Strength does NOT boost the attack that granted it; sim _inertia (skulking_colony.py:62-66) has the same order. PIERCING_STABS is a single WithHitCount(2) command on both sides (SkulkingColony.cs:88 / _execute_attack(..., 2)).
